clue.text: Herb in charge of a Roman church

parts.note: basil is a common kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A herb is put in charge of a Roman church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is an oblong aisled church, the title given to certain major Catholic churches in Rome.

clue.text: Phoenix's non-mythical state

parts.note: the phoenix of legend is a bird reborn from fire, but the real Phoenix is a city, and the state it is capital of is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is the capital city of this south-western US state.

clue.text: One comes upon many a case that can't wait'

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece coming upon another sits on top of it, so it is written first

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword stand-in for many
a doctor's case is a patient

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at the scene of many urgent cases that cannot be kept waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing apostrophe after 'wait' is an OCR speck; the page prints 'can't wait (9)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impatient is unwilling to be kept waiting.

clue.text: Are these Alpinists wild because they lack 11?

definitions.text: Are these Alpinists wild because they lack 11?

parts.words: Are these Alpinists wild because they lack 11?
parts.note: the Alpinists are not climbers but mountain goats of the Alps, and they are wild animals since no goat-keeper (the answer to 11) tends them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpinists' suggests mountaineers; it means animals that live in the Alps. The answer to 11 across is GOATHERD.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of the Alps with long curved horns.

clue.text: Barker, a Scottish volunteer ?

definitions.meaning: a barker is a dog, here the Scottish terrier breed
a terrier was slang for a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, so one from the city of Aberdeen fits

explanation.surface: A Scottish volunteer turns out to be a loudmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIER was slang for a Territorial, a part-time volunteer soldier in Britain's reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is another name for the Scottish terrier, a dog; read literally it is a reservist from the Scottish city.

clue.text: Call our attention to the gap ?

parts.note: hi is a call to get someone's notice
attention directed towards us is directed at us

explanation.surface: Someone asks us to look at a gap in the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi! At us!' is a shout calling attention to ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a break or gap, especially in a series or sequence.

clue.text: Right to inherit a Zeppelin, say ?

indicators.note: say signals the word spoken out loud, matching another word by its sound

parts.note: the Zeppelin was a German rigid airship

explanation.surface: Someone claims an inherited right to a Zeppelin.
explanation.walkthrough: With the H silent, as in heir, the answer is said like AIRSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirship is the state of being an heir, which carries the right to succeed to property.

clue.text: Falsely accuse of a terribly rude act

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the following words are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is wrongly accused of committing a very rude act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges RUDE ACT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander someone or misrepresent them maliciously.

clue.text: Dial a wild American statesman or poet

definitions.meaning: Dial a mixed up gives Adlai, the first name of the US statesman who twice ran for president against Eisenhower
Robert Louis, Scottish poet and novelist who wrote A Child's Garden of Verses

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a wild American politician or a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns DIAL A into ADLAI, pointing to Adlai Stevenson, the 1950s US presidential candidate; the same surname belongs to the poet Robert Louis Stevenson.
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous bearers of the surname: Adlai, US politician and UN ambassador, and Robert Louis, author of Treasure Island and verse.

clue.text: Simon or the one called Peter

definitions.text: Simon or the one called Peter

parts.words: Simon or the one called Peter
parts.note: it sounds like the apostle Simon called Peter, but the word wanted goes with Simon in the nursery rhyme and with Peter in the title of a Marryat novel

explanation.walkthrough: Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton; Peter Simple is Captain Marryat's naval novel. The Bible's 'Simon called Peter' is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes both names: the rhyme's foolish Simon and the hero of Marryat's 1834 novel.

clue.text: In an Arab state it's grand to leave the country

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here the letter for grand within the state

parts.note: an emirate, such as one of the United Arab Emirates, is a state ruled by an emir
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone finds life in an Arab state grand and decides to move abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to move away from one's own country to settle in another.

clue.text: In India, port by the way makes an animal tender

parts.note: Goa is a former Portuguese port and now a state on India's west coast
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A traveller in an Indian port finds a way to look after animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' here is a noun, someone who tends, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatherd is a person who looks after a flock of goats.

clue.text: Safe to see about the dog

indicators.note: about means one piece surrounds the other, so the word see wraps round the dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is safe to go and see about the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CUR inside SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure means protected from danger, the same as safe.

clue.text: Support gives relief to many

parts.note: ease is relief from pain or worry
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Giving support brings relief to many people.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painting or blackboard.

clue.text: A royal tug alone could pull it clear

definitions.text: A royal tug alone could pull it clear

parts.words: A royal tug alone could pull it clear
parts.note: in legend only the rightful king could draw a certain sword from the stone, so one royal pull frees it

explanation.walkthrough: In Arthurian legend the young Arthur proved he was king by pulling the sword from a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sword of King Arthur, drawn from the stone in some versions of the legend.

clue.text: Novices pray for second-best score at Bisley

parts.note: to pray someone for something is to beg it
Bisley is the English national shooting range; the inner is the ring next to the bull, scoring less than a bull

explanation.surface: Beginners at a shooting contest hope for a decent score.
explanation.walkthrough: BISLEY, in Surrey, is the home of British target shooting, where an inner is the ring just outside the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginners are people new to an activity, just as novices are.

clue.text: A new word for some lingo perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone coins a fresh word for a bit of jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SOME LINGO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression.

clue.text: Knight's inamorata ?

parts.note: a knight's wife takes the title Lady, and the woman a knight of romance adores is his beloved

explanation.walkthrough: The wife of a knight is styled Lady, so a knight's beloved is both his love and a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladylove is a sweetheart or beloved woman, the figure every chivalric knight serves.

clue.text: Makes shorter engagements

definitions.meaning: a verb: shrinks or reduces in length
a noun: agreements or binding undertakings

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means shrinks or shortens; as a plural noun it means legal agreements binding the parties.

clue.text: Common sense about love ? The team finds it unwholesome

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps round the next ones

parts.note: nous is British slang for practical good sense
XI is eleven, the size of a cricket or football side
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Common sense on love has a team finding the whole business distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places XI and O inside NOUS, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious means harmful or poisonous, the opposite of healthy.

clue.text: Only a fool needs a night-light ? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the night-light wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: the moon lights the night sky

explanation.surface: Only an idiot would want a night-light, someone says scornfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a night-light' sounds like a bedside lamp; it is the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: No wing has such a view

parts.note: no as a number is nought, the letter O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: No faction of the party holds such a view.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a belief or judgment, the way one sees a question.

clue.text: What Keats's beautiful lady lacked-a kingdom

parts.note: Keats wrote La Belle Dame sans Merci, the beautiful lady without mercy; merci is French for mercy

explanation.surface: Keats's beautiful lady lacked a kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: MERCIA was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the seven Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England.

clue.text: Among non-professionals ten show slackness

indicators.note: among places the number inside the group named next

parts.note: the laity are ordinary people as opposed to experts or clergy
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten amateurs in the side show a lax attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Laxity means looseness or a lack of strictness, like slackness.

clue.text: Right-hand man about to provide the necessary for a speech

indicators.note: about means the man's name wraps round the following word

parts.note: Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A trusted deputy is about to supply the essentials for a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-hand man' reads as one phrase but splits: RH, then 'man' (ERIC) placed 'about' TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, what an orator needs.

clue.text: Greens give little brother a form of colic

parts.note: bro is a short, informal word for brother

indicators.note: a form of a word is its letters arranged in another shape

explanation.surface: Green vegetables give a small boy a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a form of' rearranges COLIC into CCOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable, and greens are leafy vegetables.

clue.text: "Scorn not the Sonnet: — you have frowned" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "Scorn not the Sonnet: — you have frowned" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "Scorn not the Sonnet: — you have frowned" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: Wordsworth's sonnet addresses a scornful reviewer by title in the blank of this opening line

explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's sonnet opens 'Scorn not the Sonnet; Critic, you have frowned, / Mindless of its just honours'.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem addresses a reviewer who disparages sonnets; a reviewer who frowns on a work is a fault-finder.

clue.text: Deliver 12 perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the other answer could appear in another order

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a word meaning safe

explanation.surface: Bring the twelfth item, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is SECURE; 'perhaps' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save them.

clue.text: Back China, providing new weapons

parts.note: the rear is the back
Ming is a Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Someone supports China by arming it again.
explanation.walkthrough: MING is the Chinese dynasty, best known for its porcelain vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearming means supplying with weapons again.
